1: I taught this imperishable yoga to Vivasvān. Vivasvān told it to Manu, and Manu told it to Ikṣvāku.
2: Handed down in this way from one to the next, it was known to the royal seers. But over a great stretch of time that yoga was lost here, scorcher of foes.
3: That very same ancient yoga is what I have taught you today, because you are devoted to me and you are my friend. For this is the highest secret.
4: Your birth was later, and Vivasvān's birth was earlier. How am I to understand that you taught it in the beginning?
5: Many births of mine have passed, Arjuna, and many of yours. I know them all. You do not know them, scorcher of foes.
6: Though I am unborn and my self is imperishable, and though I am the lord of beings, I take my stand on my own nature and come into being by the illusive power of the self.
7: For whenever dharma declines, descendant of Bharata, and what is not dharma rises up, each time I send forth the self.
8: To protect the good, to destroy those who do evil, and to establish dharma, I come into being in age after age.
9: One who truly knows my divine birth and action in this way does not go to another birth on leaving the body. Such a person goes to me, Arjuna.
10: Many have come to my state of being: people whom passion, fear and anger have left, who are filled with me, who have taken refuge in me, and who are purified by the austerity of knowledge.
11: In whatever way people approach me, in just that way I receive them. Human beings follow my path in every way, son of Pṛthā.
12: Longing for their actions to succeed, people here sacrifice to the deities. For in the human world the success that is born of action comes quickly.
13: I sent forth the order of four classes, divided according to qualities and actions. Though I am its maker, know me as imperishable and as no maker.
14: Actions do not stain me, and I have no craving for the fruit of action. One who recognises me in this way is not bound by actions.
15: Knowing this, even the ancients who wished to be free did action. So you too should do action, just as the ancients did it in earlier times.
16: What is action? What is non-action? On this point even the sages are confused. I will explain that action to you, and once you know it you will be freed from what is inauspicious.
17: For there is something to be understood about action, something to be understood about wrong action, and something to be understood about non-action. The course of action runs deep.
18: One who sees non-action in action, and action in non-action, is the one among human beings who has buddhi. Such a person is joined in yoga and is a doer of all action.
19: When all of a person's undertakings are free from desire and purpose, and that person's action has been burnt by the fire of knowledge, the wise call that person learned.
20: Having given up attachment to the fruit of action, always content and depending on nothing, such a person does nothing at all, even while engaged in action.
21: Without wishes, with thought and self restrained, having given up all possessions and doing only bodily action, such a person incurs no fault.
22: Content with whatever comes by chance, beyond the pairs, free from envy, and the same in success and in failure, such a person is not bound even after acting.
23: For one whose attachment is gone, who is freed, whose mind is settled in knowledge, and who acts for sacrifice, the whole of action dissolves away.
24: Brahman is the offering and brahman is the oblation, poured by brahman into the fire of brahman. Brahman alone is to be reached by one whose samādhi is in the action of brahman.
25: Some yogīs attend only to the sacrifice to the gods. Others offer the sacrifice, by the sacrifice itself, into the fire of brahman.
26: Others offer the senses, hearing and the rest, into the fires of restraint. Others offer the objects, sound and the rest, into the fires of the senses.
27: And others offer all the actions of the senses and the actions of the breath into the fire of the yoga of restraining the self, a fire kindled by knowledge.
28: Others, likewise, make their sacrifice with material things, or with austerity, or with yoga, and others with study and knowledge. These are strivers whose vows are sharpened.
29: Others, likewise, offer the outgoing breath into the incoming breath, and the incoming breath into the outgoing. They stop the movements of the outgoing and incoming breath, intent on control of the breath.
30: Others, regulating their food, offer the breaths into the breaths. All these too know what sacrifice is, and their stains have been destroyed by sacrifice.
31: Those who eat the nectar of what remains from sacrifice go to eternal brahman. This world does not belong to one who makes no sacrifice. How then could the other, best of the Kurus?
32: In this way sacrifices of many kinds are spread out in the mouth of brahman. Know that all of them are born of action. Knowing this, you will be set free.
33: The sacrifice of knowledge is better than the sacrifice made of material things, scorcher of foes. All action, son of Pṛthā, with nothing left out, is completed in knowledge.
34: Come to know that by bowing down, by asking questions and by service. Those who have knowledge, who see the truth, will teach you knowledge.
35: Once you know it, son of Pāṇḍu, you will not fall into delusion like this again. By it you will see all beings, without exception, in the self, and then in me.
36: Even if you have done more evil than all other evildoers, you will cross over all wrong by the raft of knowledge alone.
37: As a kindled fire turns firewood to ash, Arjuna, so the fire of knowledge turns all actions to ash.
38: For no purifier equal to knowledge is found here. One who is perfected in yoga finds it in time, by oneself, in the self.
39: One who has faith gains knowledge, being intent on it and keeping the senses restrained. Having gained knowledge, such a person reaches the highest peace before long.
40: One who does not know, who has no faith, and whose self is doubt, perishes. For one whose self is doubt there is neither this world nor the other, nor happiness.
41: Actions do not bind one who has renounced actions through yoga, whose doubt has been cut apart by knowledge, and who possesses the self, winner of wealth.
42: So take the sword of knowledge and cut through this doubt of the self, which is born of ignorance and stands in the heart. Then take to yoga. Stand up, descendant of Bharata.
